163.content: Founded in 1666 by Lord Cornelius Vance Douglas, the Merchant House Douglas is the historical ancestor of the modern DCC. During the Age of Sail, they operated in London High Society under a "Respectability Mask" of legality, refinement, and noble service. However, their vast fortune was built upon the "Piracy Shadow"—ruthless privateer and pirate operations hidden in secret ledgers. This dark dynastic past established the family's enduring philosophy: reputation functions like currency, and ultimate power requires maintaining a flawless public facade while executing brutal, illicit violence in the shadows.

164.content: Long before their modern corporate empire, the Douglas-Bloodmoon lineage began in 827 AD as the Járn-Gildi (Iron Guild) clan in a mythic Norse setting of snowbound halls and iron roads. Eirikr (Erik) ruled as warlord from the Iron Keep. Before lycanthropy reshaped them, the brothers wielded ancient Seiðr magic: Logi (Logan) as a Fire-Seiðr blacksmith, Magnus (Malachia) commanding Earth-Seiðr, and Njal (Noah) utilizing Name-Truth binding. Guided by Wulfnic "Ulfr", this dark fantasy era laid the brutal, unbreakable foundations of their modern pack loyalty.

165.content: In the dystopian cyberpunk future of 2375, the Douglas Commercial Coalition evolves into Bloodmoon Industries, a multi-planetary "corporate pack" ruling over 80 star systems. Erik reigns as the Alpha CEO ("The Tyrant"), enforcing the oppressive "BlackMoon Pack Law" via inescapable biometric tracking and monolithic brutalist towers. Noah acts as the ruthless legal liaison, while Malachia commands the Vanguard PMC. The only refuge from this luxury cyberpunk panopticon is the Underground, where Logan runs the "Verve Safe Garage"—an analog, biometric blind spot for rebels and outcasts.

166.content: Hidden beneath the layers of modern urban fantasy lies the myth of Amarantia, the lost city of magic from the ancient 'Era della Foglia'. It is secretly guarded and remembered by descendants of "The Guardians," an ancient military magic order divided into elemental disciplines (Fire, Water, Light, Shadow, Earth). While mostly relegated to myth, fragments of this high magic still circulate in the modern underworld, heavily guarded by ancient beings who predate the werewolf packs.

919723.content: Category: WORLD CONCEPT. The supernatural ecosystem of Blackwood extends beyond wolves and vampires. The 'Fracture' allows minor European folklore entities to bleed into the urban decay. Symbiotic Daimons bind to humans for psychic exchange; Domovoy (hearth spirits) fiercely protect ancestral homes; Meliae (ash-tree nymphs) and the horrific White Lady (Winter Goddess) hunt in the frozen fringes. Minuscule Kobolds and Knockers relentlessly dismantle technological scrap in the industrial sectors. These entities function as the lethal background noise of the world, maintaining the ancient, superstitious dread of the Dark Urban Fantasy setting without actively challenging the dominant power structures of the Packs or the Vampire Court.

919724.content: Category: WORLD CONCEPT. Since Blackwood's werewolves originated from the ancient Viking myth of the Úlfhéðnar (Berserkers who became wolves by wearing their skins), all creatures and deities from Norse mythology are entirely real within the Svartúlfr universe. Much like the 'American Gods' or 'Being Human' universes, these ancient beings have evolved and adapted to modern society to survive. A Nøkken might perform hypnotic sets in a dark underground club; a Hulder might use her glamour as an influencer while hiding her hollow back; and a Draugr might serve as an immovable security guard for a corporate vault. They exist in the hidden fabric of the modern world, blending ancient magic with contemporary urban decay.
